Variables.basisOfRecord_reasoning: The study involved collecting ants and spiders using specific sampling methods (Winkler traps, entomological umbrella, manual capture) and subsequently depositing the specimens in specialized collections (Laboratório de Mirmecologia and Instituto Butantan) for identification and analysis.
Variables.measurementMethod: Sampling involved Winkler traps (50x50 cm units, 24h) for soil fauna, entomological umbrellas (1 m2, 10s) for vegetation fauna, and manual diurnal capture (15 min). Species were identified and classified into functional groups based on specific criteria: for ants, features included trophic position, nest/foraging location, worker recruitment mode, and morphology; for spiders, criteria included time of capture, foraging site, foraging mode, web use, and web type. Species richness was estimated using the Jackknife 1 estimator, and community composition was analyzed using Nonmetric Multidimensional Scaling (NMDS) ordination with the Bray-Curtis index.
